entities.name: PMID:10729388
observations: Population-based case-control study in Northern Ireland: 259 myocardial infarction cases aged 25–70 years and 259 population-based controls from the same area.
CagA IgG seropositivity was 56.4% in cases versus 47.9% in controls; crude OR 1.41, 95% CI 1.00–1.99.
After adjustment for age, sex, number of siblings, smoking, and socioeconomic-status measures, OR was 1.16, 95% CI 0.79–1.70.
Authors concluded that infection with virulent CagA-positive H. pylori strains, like infection with all strains, was not associated with myocardial infarction.

entities.name: Null adjusted association
observations: In the Northern Ireland population-based case-control study, the apparent crude association between CagA-positive H. pylori infection and myocardial infarction was substantially attenuated after confounder adjustment and was not statistically significant (adjusted OR 1.16, 95% CI 0.79–1.70).

entities.name: CagA-positive H. pylori
observations: CagA-positive strains were used as the marker of more virulent Helicobacter pylori infection in the study.

entities.name: Myocardial infarction
observations: Outcome examined in the population-based case-control study of virulent H. pylori infection.
